To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated a simple route to synthesize metallic, semiconductive or semi-metallic InSb nanocrystals by controlling temperature and vapor pressure in the high eutectic temperature range of the InSbmelt phase diagram.

we have demonstrated a new method to synthesize metallic In, semiconductng InSb, and semi-metalic Sb nanowires by controling the growth temperature and the Sb vapor pressure in a narrow temperature window of the InSbs phase diagram.

we have developed a simple method to control InSb growth in the higher eutectic region of the In–Sb phase diagram, which results in growth of metallic In, semiconductiing InSb and semi-metallic Sb nanowires.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new nanowire synthesis techniques and the characterization of their electronic properties.
the growth and characterization of InSb, In and Sb nanowires, which have been synthesized by controlling growth temperature.
the growth and electronic characterization of InSb, In and Sb nanowires by CVD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a new method to synthesize metallic, semiconductive and semi-metallic semiconductor nanowires.
the growth of In, InSb and Sb nanowires is possible by simply controlling the Sb vapor pressure in a narrow temperature range in the higher euctectic region of InSb phase-diagram.
the InSb nanorod morphology and electrical properties can be controlled through the growth conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nanowire growth process is highly sensitive to growth conditions and that the resulting nanowires can have very different electrical properties.
the nanowire growth process is highly sensitive to temperature and the vapor pressures of the constituent elements.
by controlling the growth conditions, it is possible to grow nanowires of different compositions and hence electronic properties, which can then be used to build devices with different functionality.

by controlling growth temperature and hence vapor pressure of antimony in the higher eutectic region of the In–Sb phase diagram, we can grow metallic In, semiconductinig InSb, and semi-metalic Sb nanowires.
by controlling the growth parameters, we can tune the electrical conductivity of nanowires grown by the same growth process.
